findings.description: The fast-path guard is inverted. It returns the maximum wait whenever the exponent is below the overflow threshold, when it should only do so once the exponential has reached or passed max.
findings.rationale: Trigger: wait_exponential(multiplier=1, max=100, exp_base=2) on attempt 1 gives exponent 0, which is less than log(100, 2) ≈ 6.64, so the early return yields max(0, 100) = 100 seconds instead of the correct 1 second. Mechanism: for every small attempt number the function skips the real computation and returns max. Impact: users get wait times clamped to max from the first retry onward, so backoff is effectively disabled and retries are far too slow.
